title: Framework-centric Architecture (Invasive Architecture)
pattern: Basing the entire core application architecture on a specific framework, allowing framework-specific constructs to dominate the domain model.
why_bad: An invasive architecture overwhelms the domain logic, making stories harder to implement, testing difficult without running heavy container mock suites, and compromising TDD velocity.
detection: Direct imports or types from web/web-socket/persistence frameworks in the signatures of core business logic routines.
counterexample: Web handlers that extract parameters from requests and immediately pass native types to pure business functions.
fix: Define business policies as Plain Old Objects (POJOs/POCOs) with clean boundaries, keeping the framework on the outer circles.
